stages.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE new full-bleed opening background for the mature Nur Islam mobile app, the DAYLIGHT master of a five-time-of-day series. Image 1 is the old mosque courtyard, SUBJECT reference only; replace its photographic ornate rendering. Image 2 is our approved mosque illustration, PRIMARY MATERIAL/SHAPE STYLE reference: simple clean ivory walls, deep teal dome, muted olive accents, restrained gold, smooth matte satin 3D forms, clear gentle shading. Image 3 is our own garden scene, matching ENVIRONMENT RENDER STYLE only. Build a calm coherent grown-up 3D illustrated courtyard environment, not a toy, not photorealistic, not excessively rounded childish architecture. A small elegant ivory mosque with one teal dome and two complete slender minarets, simple clean entrance and a few uncluttered arcades. Camera frontal and distant. CRITICAL RESPONSIVE FRAMING: landscape 3:2 canvas, huge quiet light-blue sky in the upper 72% for actual app text added in code. ALL mosque architecture, including BOTH minaret tips, MUST fit within the CENTRAL x=36%-64% of the full canvas and y=74%-96% of canvas. The building must occupy ONLY the middle 28% width: this is deliberate so portrait phone cropping shows the ENTIRE mosque and both minarets. Outside that central lower building, show only a simple continuous ivory courtyard ground meeting a low flat horizon at y94%, no side buildings stretching out to the frame. No palm trees or shrubs at the edges. No clouds or sun in the central text zone x30%-70%, y10%-70%; a couple of soft understated clouds far outside the central column are fine. Clear neutral MIDDAY daylight, soft warm ivory stone, calm natural blue sky, teal dome, small gold accents. No ornate filigree, no calligraphy, no written words, no humans, no logo or watermark, no UI, no extra border/frame. Do not enlarge the architecture to fill the wide frame: the small centered mosque in a huge quiet sky is an essential mobile-safe composition. One final image.

stages.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target, our just-created stylized mosque courtyard for a phone opening. Keep the same 3D design, colors, lighting and quiet blue sky. Correct the scale and position ONLY. The current mosque is too tall and high. SCALE THE ENTIRE MOSQUE, including both minarets, facade, side arcades, steps and all roof decorations, DOWN TO 55% of its present width and height. Keep it centered at x50%, then MOVE IT DOWN until the bottom step is at y96% of the whole canvas. After this transformation the very highest minaret tip should be at about y75%, and the entire mosque should occupy approximately x39%-61%, y75%-96%. No mosque dome, tower, wall or other object above y74%. The foreground courtyard should meet a low horizon around y94%, with plain sky above it. Fill the area formerly occupied by the tall mosque seamlessly with blue sky. Maintain the full-bleed landscape 3:2 canvas, calm mature matte 3D materials. This small distant lower-center architecture is REQUIRED so all central Arabic/German app text stays over the SKY and the complete mosque fits a narrow portrait crop. No text or UI. No new props or people. Do not enlarge the mosque again to fill the image.

Edit Image 1. Keep the canvas, sky, courtyard floor, colors, architecture design and lighting unchanged. Make the mosque MUCH smaller: HALF its CURRENT width and HALF its CURRENT height, scaling the entire mosque including both minarets and steps together around the bottom-center point where the entrance steps touch the courtyard. Keep that bottom contact at exactly the same position in the image. It should now look like a much more DISTANT small mosque at the bottom-center. The highest tower must end in the bottom QUARTER of the image. Fill all vacated space above and around the reduced mosque with the existing blue sky. Do not move the small mosque upward or zoom back in afterward. Full image framing remains identical. No new objects, no writing. This is a functional app background requiring the upper three quarters to be empty sky.
